name: Silver Fir of Santa Maria del Bosco

location.address: Santuario di Santa Maria del Bosco, Serra San Bruno (VV)

location_site.name: Santa Maria del Bosco sanctuary forecourt

official_register.name: Elenco degli alberi monumentali d'Italia (MASAF), sheet 03/I639/VV/18

access: Free. The comune describes the sanctuary complex (large forecourt, Saint Bruno's small lake, granite staircase up to the church) as the main visitor draw of Serra San Bruno, tens of thousands of visitors in summer. Church entry is free by the front staircase; check opening hours before you go. The Certosa monastery itself is closed to visitors; the sanctuary and woods are not part of it.
transport: About 2 km from the Certosa entrance on foot or by car (Certosa car park). No railway; Serra San Bruno has local buses, check the timetable.
verify_notes: Register-only for the individual tree: MASAF 03/I639/VV/18, Silver Fir, 390 cm girth, 33 m, locality Santa Maria del Bosco. Second source is partial: the comune says the sanctuary stands among secular silver firs and young beeches; an iNaturalist research-grade Abies alba observation (2021-11-05, obs 101131944, not openly licensed, no accuracy given) lies about 12 m from the register point, so a fir does stand at that spot. Nothing names THIS trunk. RECOGNISE: the register point is inside the sanctuary complex, in the fir wood around the forecourt by the lake of San Bruno and the granite staircase; the biggest fir in that forecourt is the one to look for (no source describes the trunk, so the writer should not invent marks). ALIVE: 2021 iNaturalist sighting only; flag. Rule change 2026-11-02: approximate pin ships. Context: the comune page places the Dormitory of San Bruno on the far side of the sanctuary.
story:
Serra San Bruno's most visited place is a church in a fir wood, and Italy's national register picks out one of those firs as monumental. It is a silver fir 33 metres tall with a trunk 390 centimetres round, at Santa Maria del Bosco, the sanctuary in the woods about two kilometres from the town's Carthusian monastery.

The comune describes the sanctuary standing among secular silver firs and young beeches, with a large forecourt, the small lake of Saint Bruno and a granite staircase up to the church. Tens of thousands of people come in summer. Bosco means wood, and these firs are it.

The monastery itself is closed to visitors. The sanctuary and its woods are not part of the enclosure, and the church is reached freely by its front staircase.

The register gives the size but no description of the trunk, and no source dates it, so how old it is remains a question. A fir stood at this spot in a 2021 observation, but we have found nothing more recent. If you go, look for the biggest fir around the forecourt and tell us what you find.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the biggest silver fir around the sanctuary forecourt, 33 metres tall and nearly 4 metres round, in the wood by Saint Bruno's lake and the granite staircase.

name: Silver Fir of Monte Pecoraro

location.address: Monte Pecoraro, Serre Calabresi (Serra San Bruno / Mongiana)

official_register.name: Elenco degli alberi monumentali d'Italia (MASAF), sheet 09/I639/VV/18

access: Free; forest tracks in the Parco Naturale Regionale delle Serre. Parco delle Serre trail Pecoraro-Lu Bellu (7.5 km, about 3 h, medium) starts at the ANAS cantoniera on SS 110 and runs through beech and fir woods; a guided hike to Monte Pecoraro was advertised for 24 Oct 2026 (Calabria Tour page). Walking only; no facilities.
transport: By car to the ANAS cantoniera of Pecoraro on the SS 110 (Stilo / Mongiana side, about 1,300 m); no public transport found.
verify_notes: Register: MASAF 09/I639/VV/18, 480 cm, 45 m. A local walking association (Vivi Serra San Bruno, lacnews24 2022-07-23) runs hikes to Monte Pecoraro 'where one of the largest white firs in Europe stands'; Calabria Tour (2026) describes firs of nearly 50 m on the way to the summit, 1,423 m, highest point of the Serre, with a historic lookout tower. The 45 m figure is the register's and is tall for Abies alba but plausible for the Serre. RECOGNISE: sources do not say which fir; the register point lies below the summit on the Pecoraro side (38.541, 16.3427); the writer should say it is the biggest fir by the path and not invent marks. PIN is only the register point. ALIVE: association hike 2022 and 2026 tour name the area, not this trunk; flag. Possible confusion with the Mongiana 'albero delle fate' (6 m girth, 35 m, lacnews24) which is a different tree.
hold: cannot be told apart: no source says which fir on Monte Pecoraro is the register tree, register point only

name: Silver Fir of Rosarella

official_register.name: Elenco degli alberi monumentali d'Italia (MASAF), sheet 05/I639/VV/18

access: Free. The Archiforo trail (4 km, about 2 h, medium) of the Parco delle Serre starts at the car park by the Rosarella botanical garden and nursery and enters the Archiforo fir and beech wood at a signed information board; marked path with fences and footbridges.
transport: Rosarella is on the south-east edge of Serra San Bruno town; by car or about a 20 to 30 min walk (not measured).
verify_notes: Register-only for the tree: MASAF 05/I639/VV/18, 470 cm, 30 m, locality Rosarella. The park authority's Archiforo page puts a signed trail and the Rosarella nursery at this locality in the same fir and beech wood, but does not name this tree, so existence of THIS fir is single-source. RECOGNISE: look near the Rosarella nursery fence and trail start; no source describes the trunk. ALIVE: no dated sighting; flag. A non-open iNaturalist Abies alba fix (2025-12-07) lies about 50 m away, not tied to this trunk.
hold: cannot be told apart: the Rosarella trail page names no tree, register point only
